closest_biobased_competitor.name: Green Boom B0510S
closest_biobased_competitor.key_point: Bio-based hydrophobic, marine, retrievable and wring/reuse concepts already exist commercially. SCOBY must win by cost/performance/feedstock route, not by biodegradability alone.

janus_tranception.forward: SCOBY_SOURCE -> PROCESS_COST -> MARINE_q -> RETRIEVE -> PRESS -> RECOVERED_OIL -> TOTAL_COST_PER_RECOVERED_KG -> MARKET
janus_tranception.reverse: MARKET_PRICE_CEILING -> MAX_TOTAL_COST -> PROCESS_HEADROOM -> REQUIRED_q_X_RECOVERY -> MAX_BC_COST -> SCOBY_SOURCE

preliminary_output: At central dry-BC cost, q≈20 g/g is borderline against cheapest polypropylene once processing is added; q≈40 g/g is the practical economic target. If SCOBY is a genuinely low-cost byproduct, q≈20 g/g can already be economically interesting. Against the closest bio-based Green Boom analogue, q>=20 g/g shows plausible raw-material advantage, but total processed cost must be measured.
next_gate: Test SCOBY and a cheap PP control under one frozen marine protocol; ideally add Green Boom as the bio-based control. Report total cost per actually recovered kg oil, not nominal capacity.
